Deja's Most Moving Moments on This Is Us

She has so many incredible scenes!

During its six-season run, This Is Us painted a nuanced portrait of familial love and dysfunction that millions of people could relate to. While the dynamics between the Big Three was at the center of the story, several standout characters brought even more heart to the narrative, including Beth and Randall's adopted daughter, Deja (Lyric Ross). Here are just a few of her most moving moments on the show.

Season 2, Episode 4 ("Still There")

Deja didn't have an easy life before she was taken in by Randall and Beth. So, it totally made sense that the spirited survivor was slow to trust and open up. However, when Deja was vulnerable with Beth by letting her braid her hair, it hit audiences hard. The scene reaches an emotional fever pitch when we discover that Deja suffers from hair loss due to alopecia.

Season 2, Episode 10 ("Number Three")

After Deja's mom shows up unannounced to let the Pearsons know she's seeking custody, the story takes one sad turn after another. The tear-jerker deals one final blow when the time comes for Deja to say goodbye to Randall and Beth—and let me tell you, it was crushing.

Season 2, Episode 17 ("This Big, Amazing, Beautiful Life")

After Deja's difficult goodbye earlier in Season 2, fans were relieved to have her back in the Pearson household when her biological mother permanently relinquishes her parental rights. During this episode via a beautiful monologue, Deja confides in Randall about how drained she is by all the different living situations she's had.

Season 3, Episode 1 ("Nine Bucks")

Deja finds and confronts her biological father in the Season 3 premiere. She reveals to the absent parent that she's come to terms with his decision to forfeit his role in her life and has found a new family with parents who think she's "exceptional." All she needs from her biological father is for him to grant the Pearsons the authority to be her legal guardians. Watching Deja navigate this painful, sobering, and adult interaction will definitely pull at your heartstrings.

Not a Great Bet is the seventh episode of Season 4 and the 43rd overall episode.

Summary[]

Gretchen goes home for the birth of her brother's baby, but instead ends up reconnecting with a friend from her past who inadvertently reveals why Jimmy may have left her.

Cast[]

Main Cast[]

- Chris Geere as Jimmy Shive-Overly (Credit Only)

- Aya Cash as Gretchen Cutler

- Desmin Borges as Edgar Quintero (Credit Only)

- Kether Donohue as Lindsay Jillian (Credit Only)

Plot[]

The episode follows Gretchen as she goes to her parents' home for the birth of her brother's first child.

She discovers that her 8th grade friend Heidi (Zosia Mamet) survived leukemia and now owns their old roller rink hangout.

Avoiding her familial duties, she reconnects with Heidi. Heidi does not share her enthusiasm, but they both go an old derelict mall to drink and smoke.

They find some stressed out teenagers just hanging out and try to get them to loosen up.

The police raid the mall and they escape in Gretchen's rented pickup, abandoning it in a corn field. As they walk home,

Gretchen says she wants to stay in town with Heidi, but Heidi says they were never friends after middle school as Gretchen was so unstable. Gretchen yells abuse at Heidi as she walks away.

Gretchen finally arrives at the hospital, peeks in at her family with the new baby, and leaves.
